We lend against cattle you could go and count.

SV Capital is an asset-backed private lending fund. We do one thing: we finance commercial cattle in South Africa, and the herd is the security. Your money is lent, for a set period, against animals that exist, in a feedlot you could drive to, with a buyer already contracted to take them.

Nine years of it, since our first cattle pool. It is not a fund of funds, not an index, and not a note written off someone else’s balance sheet.

How the lending works

Four steps. Nothing in it is complicated — it is a herd, a feedlot, a contract and a sale, in that order.

  1. The money buys cattle

    Your capital, pooled with other lenders, buys weaners into a commercial feedlot. Real animals under a named operator — not a share in a cattle price and not a paper exposure to farming.

  2. The herd is the security

    The animals themselves stand behind the loan. They are insured against disease, theft and natural hazards, and while they are in the feedlot the veterinary and biosecurity obligations sit with the operator — Beefcor, one of the largest feedlot businesses in the country.

  3. The buyer is contracted before we start

    The cattle are sold on to Beefcor for finishing, under an offtake agreement negotiated before the pool opens. This is the part worth understanding: the price the herd leaves at is settled up front, so the pool is not left taking whatever the market offers on the day it has to sell.

  4. You are repaid when the cycle closes

    About 120 days, then capital and return come back together. The cattle have to reach weight and the offtake has to be honoured. Capital is at risk, any rate quoted beforehand is a target rather than a promise, and what you are paid is what the pool achieved.

What has already been paid back

Those are cattle pools that have closed out — capital and return already in lenders’ hands, not projections. Past performance is not a guide to future returns, and no pool guarantees one.

How it goes, from your side

Five steps, in this order, every time.

  1. A conversation

    What you are trying to do with the money, over what period, and what you need to see while it is working. Past the entry point nothing else is quoted off a list, because it would be a guess about your situation.

  2. An agreement in writing

    Naming both parties, the pool, the term and the basis the return is calculated on. SmartVest Financial Services (Pty) Ltd is the authorised provider; SV Capital is the fund manager. Nothing is deployed before this is signed.

  3. Your money goes into a named pool

    One pool, one herd, one transaction — not a general account. Each pool stands on its own and settles on its own.

  4. Reporting while it runs

    A factsheet each reporting period for the pool you are in, and a login that shows your own position. Figures are posted against what the pool did, never projected forward from a rate.

  5. Repayment at the end of the term

    Capital and return, with a statement setting out how each figure was arrived at.

About SV Capital

We are a South African asset-backed lender. We have been financing commercial cattle for nine years, since our first pool, and it is the business we know best.

Who holds the licence

SmartVest Financial Services (Pty) Ltd, an authorised financial services provider, FSP 52449, regulated by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority. Every rand in and every rand out runs through it. SV Capital is the fund manager and administers each pool under that licence.

How you are onboarded

Full FICA and AML onboarding, the same know-your-client work whatever the size of the allocation. It is not a formality we skip for larger clients.

Who we work with

Beefcor, one of the largest commercial feedlot operators in South Africa, both feeds the herd and contracts to buy it. We do not open a pool against a counterparty that has not been through our diligence.

Questions people ask before they commit

Is my capital guaranteed?

No, and anybody who tells you otherwise about an asset-backed loan is selling you something. Capital is at risk. What we can tell you is what secures it, who is buying the herd, and what has happened in the pools that have already closed.

How much do I need to place?

R1 000 000. That is the entry point for a private-client relationship — terms agreed with you, reporting to suit, and somebody who answers the phone. Above it, size is still settled in conversation rather than off a price list. There is nothing on this page to click: should you wish to invest, contact us and we will take it from there.

Can I get out early?

Generally no. The money is lent against a real herd with a real end date, and the term exists because the cattle have to be finished and the buyer has to pay. Choose the term deliberately; that is part of the first conversation.

Who is actually responsible for my money?

SmartVest Financial Services (Pty) Ltd, an authorised financial services provider, FSP 52449. SV Capital is the fund manager and administers each pool under that licence. Both are named in your agreement.

What does the rate mean before a pool closes?

It is a target, drawn from the underlying trade, and it is labelled as one. Once a pool closes out, what it actually returned is what is shown.

Do you work through my adviser or accountant?

Yes, including reporting addressed to them. If you allocate for an institution or advise other people’s clients, the institutional page is written for that.
